etymologies.etymologyHTML: From dragon +‎ fly.

definitions.definition: An insect of the suborder Epiprocta or, more strictly, the infraorder Anisoptera, having four long transparent wings held perpendicular to a long body when perched.

quote.text: The delicate coloured Dragon Flies may have likewise some Corrosive quality.

quote.citation: 1897, Thomas Wright, The Acid Sisters: And Other Poems, page 93:
quote.text: The sapphire needled dragonflies That flirt with the crested newt! And now before his newtly nose,  […]

quote.citation: 2013 April 1, Natalie Angier, “Nature’s Drone, Pretty and Deadly”, in The New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: Stacey Combes, who studies the biomechanics of dragonfly flight at Harvard, once watched a laboratory dragonfly eat 30 flies in a row.

quote.citation: 2016 June 11, Lizette Alvarez, “In a Corner of the Everglades, a Way of Life Ebbs”, in The New York Times‎[2]:
quote.text: As the airboat skimmed across the shallow water, scattering blue dragonflies and launching a heron into the air, Keith Price squinted into the sun and relished the isolation of Florida’s unrivaled river of grass.
